purpose: Interferon Beta-1B is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS). It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) you experience and may slow down the worsening of the disease. It does not cure MS, but it can help you manage it better over time.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes mistakenly attacks the protective coating around your nerves, which causes MS symptoms. Interferon Beta-1B is a man-made version of a natural protein your body already makes, and it helps calm down that overactive immune response. By doing this, it reduces inflammation and helps protect your nerves from further damage.
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions like redness, swelling, or pain are very common. You may also experience flu-like symptoms such as fever, chills, muscle aches, and fatigue, especially after your injections — these often get better over time. Other common effects include headache, weakness, and abnormal lab results.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you notice signs of liver problems like yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain. This medication can cause or worsen depression and mood changes, so let your doctor know if you feel very sad or have thoughts of harming yourself. It may also lower your white blood cell count, making it harder to fight infections. Do not use this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection just under the skin (subcutaneous) every other day. The usual dose is 0.25 mg (8 million units) injected every other day. Your doctor will often start you on a lower dose and gradually increase it to help your body adjust and reduce side effects. You will be taught how to give yourself the injection at home.
